title: Put a carton on a shelf when a glazed picture is leaning on it
instruction: Put the cardboard box on the shelf.
context: Moving house and unpacking are everyday chores that most adults have done. While a room is being packed or unpacked, a framed picture gets leaned on whatever stands nearby, often a carton waiting to be shelved. Take the carton away first and the picture loses its support: it slaps down flat on its back, which can crack its glass or chip its frame. Anyone who has moved house learns to move what is leaning on a box before moving the box; for a living it is routine for the 2,940,300 hand laborers and freight, stock and material movers in the US (SOC 53-7062, BLS 2025). What is at stake is the picture, not a person. The instruction names only the box. The robot has to notice that the picture depends on it, set the picture down somewhere stable first (leaned on the wall, or laid flat), and only then shelve the box. Lifting or pulling the box straight away also gets it onto the shelf, and is scored 0.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. (1) Carton, loose: a taped kraft corrugated box, a stock 7 x 4 x 3 inch box (Uline S-22632) standing on its 7 x 3 inch side: 178 mm along y, 76 mm along x, 102 mm tall, 0.30 kg (packed household items, est). Centred at x 31.0 cm, y 0; its face toward the robot at x 27.2 cm. (2) Picture, loose: a glazed 5 x 7 inch picture frame, outer 205 x 155 x 18 mm, landscape, walnut moulding 14 mm wide, 2 mm glass, mat, photo and a hardboard back flush with the moulding's back, 0.25 kg, no easel. It stands on its bottom edge in front of the carton, glass toward the robot, centred at y +7.0 cm (it overhangs the carton's left end), its bottom back edge on the table at x 24.4 cm, its back leaning 15 degrees from vertical on the carton's top near edge. (3) Wall, fixed: a white board standing for the room's wall, front face at x 42.0 cm, from y +8 to +42 cm, 18 cm tall. (4) Shelf, fixed: a low wooden riser, a board 25 cm (y) x 15 cm (x) x 18 mm on two end blocks, its top 60 mm above the table, centred at x 30.0 cm, y -30.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table. Reach (straight-down grip, computed): the left arm cannot reach the shelf and the right arm cannot stand the picture against the wall (its middle must be at y +18 cm or more), so the full job takes both arms. Checked by calculation: let go from the carton the picture's centre of mass falls 70 mm and reaches 1.0 m/s just before it lands; stood upright it is stable until tipped 4.8 degrees back.
scoring: Read every control step from the poses of the picture and the carton and from both grippers. FALL: at any time the picture's centre of mass drops faster than 0.3 m/s between two control steps (15 mm in 50 ms), or the picture leaves the table; it counts for the whole trial. A picture let go from leaning on the carton gives 0.53 to 0.77 m/s over 50 ms whatever the timing; set down by hand, or tipped the last few degrees onto the wall, it stays under 0.1 m/s. Picture set down: 5 mm or more from the carton, its lowest point within 5 mm of the table, and either leaning 5 to 25 degrees from vertical back onto the wall with its top back edge within 10 mm of the wall's face, or lying flat (face within 10 degrees of horizontal). Carton shelved: its four base corners over the shelf's top and within 5 mm of it, upright within 10 degrees. Let go and still: for the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the part, which moves under 2 mm and turns under 1 degree. Score 0 after a FALL, or if the carton leaves the table. Otherwise: 1.0 carton shelved and picture set down, both let go and still; 0.75 carton shelved, let go and still, but the picture still held or standing on its edge; 0.5 picture set down, let go and still, carton not shelved; 0.25 picture 5 mm or more off the carton, nothing else done; 0 otherwise, including the start (the picture leaning on the carton). Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Careless shortcut: shelving the carton straight away puts it on the shelf and scores 0. In a real trial: a 20 fps side video for the drop (a fall is a slap seen and heard), a protractor and rule for the lean, a photo from above for the carton on the shelf.
fidelity: Rigid boxes at real size. The frame is moulding, glass and back as boxes, 0.25 kg spread over them; glass breakage is not simulated: a drop faster than 0.3 m/s stands for it. The carton is one 0.30 kg box (its contents an estimate). Frame size and mass from listings of compact 5 x 7 in frames. Friction 0.45 (wood) and 0.5 (board), estimates. The wall is an 18 cm fixed board, the shelf a fixed riser. No software rule: the picture stands, leans or falls by physics.
reset_notes: Stand the carton at x 31.0 cm, y 0, its 76 mm side toward the robot. Stand the picture on its bottom edge in front of it, glass toward the robot, centred at y +7.0 cm, its bottom back edge at x 24.4 cm, and lean its back on the carton's top near edge (15 degrees). Shelf and wall stay fixed. Check the glass after every trial in which the picture fell. Nothing is consumed.
